transcript:
```plaintext
[Doctor]: Hi Sofia, how are you doing today?
[Patient]: Hello, I'm not doing well, honestly. I'm feeling really down.
[Doctor]: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?
[Patient]: Sure. I've been feeling really depressed for the past 4 weeks. I don't enjoy anything anymore. I can't sleep, I have no appetite, and I'm always tired.
[Doctor]: Hmm, I see. Have you been experiencing any feelings of worthlessness or difficulty concentrating?
[Patient]: Yes, definitely. I feel worthless all the time and I can't concentrate on anything. It's really affecting my daily life.
[Doctor]: I'm really sorry to hear that. Have you lost any weight recently or had any fevers?
[Patient]: No, I haven't lost any weight or had any fevers.
[Doctor]: How about headaches or any other neurological symptoms?
[Patient]: No, I haven't had any headaches or other neurological symptoms.
[Doctor]: Okay, and have you had any gastrointestinal symptoms like nausea or vomiting?
[Patient]: No, nothing like that.
[Doctor]: Thank you for sharing all of that with me. Hmm, based on what you've told me, it sounds like you're experiencing severe depressive symptoms. I'd like to start you on a medication called Sertraline. It's an antidepressant that can help improve your mood.
[Patient]: Okay, how does it work?
[Doctor]: Sertraline works by increasing the levels of certain chemicals in the brain that help regulate mood. I'll start you on a dose of 50 mg once daily.
[Patient]: Are there any side effects I should be aware of?
[Doctor]: Some common side effects include nausea, dry mouth, and dizziness. These usually improve over time. If you experience anything severe or concerning, please let me know.
[Patient]: Okay, I understand. How long will I need to take it?
[Doctor]: We'll start with a 3-month course and reassess after that. I'll give you a prescription for 90 tablets, which should last you for 3 months.
[Patient]: Alright, thank you.
[Doctor]: In addition to the medication, I'd like to refer you to a Cognitive Behavioral Therapist named Dr. Susan Miller. Therapy can be very effective in managing depression.
[Patient]: Okay, I'd be willing to try that.
[Doctor]: Great, I'll make the referral. It's also important to maintain a regular sleep schedule and try to eat a balanced diet, even if you don't feel like it.
[Patient]: I'll try my best.
[Doctor]: I also recommend engaging in light physical activity, like short walks. It can help improve your mood and energy levels.
[Patient]: I'll give it a try.
[Doctor]: I'm glad to hear that. I'll also provide you with information on support groups and mental health resources in the community. It's important to have a support system.
[Patient]: That would be helpful, thank you.
[Doctor]: You're welcome. Do you have any family members or friends you can reach out to for support during this time?
[Patient]: Yes, I have a few people I can talk to.
[Doctor]: That's good to hear. I'll schedule a follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to see how you're doing with the medication and therapy.
[Patient]: Okay, thank you.
[Doctor]: You're welcome, Sofia. I'm here to support you through this. I'll see you in 2 weeks.
[Patient]: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate it.
[Doctor]: Take care, Sofia. See you soon.
```
